question: Which among the following NOT a pharmacological action of opioids
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Opioids" -> "activation of mu receptors in the brain" -> "suppression of the cough reflex" -> "Cough suppression" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Opioids" -> "stimulation of chemoreceptor trigger zone" -> "increased nausea and vomiting" -> "Anti-emesis" is incorrect -> 90%
CHAIN: "Opioids" -> "activation of opioid receptors in the CNS" -> "constriction of the pupil" -> "Miosis" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Opioids" -> "activation of opioid receptors in the CNS" -> "increased muscle tone" -> "Truncal rigidity" -> 90%
analysis: Opioids are known to have several pharmacological effects including analgesia, cough suppression, and causing miosis (pupil constriction). They are also associated with causing nausea and vomiting in some cases, but they can be used in the management of vomiting under certain conditions. However, opioids are known to cause muscle rigidity, including truncal rigidity, which is a well-documented side effect, particularly with high doses or rapid administration. Therefore, the statement that opioids have an anti-emetic effect (reduce vomiting) is not typically accurate as their primary action can actually induce vomiting.
